title: Intelligence — cache hit rate, score recompute, reads (§19)

panels.title: Cache hit rate, by cache
panels.description: risk_score / labels cache-aside hit rate — hit / (hit + miss). A dropping rate means Redis is degraded or the model version just rolled (invalidating every cached score).

panels.title: Score recompute latency p50 / p99 (s)
panels.description: The live risk_scorer::load_risk_inputs + risk::score path, sampled only on a risk-score cache miss.

panels.title: Entity graph / timeline requests, by found
Entity graph truncations, by reason
panels.description: A walk that stopped short of its requested hops — the degree-cap/hub-node discipline (§8.2) in action.

panels.title: Seed ingest (labels/sanctions), most recent run
panels.description: OFAC/EU list ingestion — production_readiness.md's sanctions-freshness SLA depends on this running on schedule.

panels.title: Similarity searches, by outcome
panels.description: §20.3 behavioral similarity. `no_baseline` climbing is the alert — it is the one failure that looks like a normal empty answer from outside the service, and it means the `intelligence embedding-baseline` run mode has stopped. `no_signal` is a property of the queried addresses, not of the system.

panels.title: Similarity searches hitting the shortlist cap
panels.description: Share of served searches whose candidate shortlist filled its cap, so a better neighbour may exist outside it. The shortlist ranks in raw cosine space and the score re-ranks in baseline-standardized space, so this is the recall knob's feedback signal — a high share means raising INTEL_SIMILARITY_CANDIDATE_MULTIPLIER.

panels.title: Population baseline age (§20.3)
panels.description: How old the baseline every similarity score is standardized against actually is. THIS IS THE SILENT FAILURE: if the `intelligence embedding-baseline` run mode dies, nothing errors — searches keep returning confident rankings against a population that is drifting away from reality. Alert above roughly two refresh intervals; past INTEL_SIMILARITY_BASELINE_MAX_AGE_SECS the search is refused outright (outcome=no_baseline on the panel above).

panels.title: Baseline refresh outcomes
panels.description: Refreshes of the process-wide baseline snapshot. A sustained `error` rate alongside a climbing age is the signature of 'ClickHouse is up but behavior_baselines is not readable'. Sustained `missing` means the baseline job has never produced one for this (chain, version).

panels.title: Neighbour cache outcomes (materialized rankings)
panels.description: The address_neighbors read model. `stale_baseline` spiking ONCE right after a baseline re-derivation is correct — that is the fingerprint invalidation doing its job. A SUSTAINED stale_baseline rate means baselines are being rewritten faster than the working set refills, and the cache is costing more than it saves: widen INTEL_SIMILARITY_BASELINE_REFRESH_SECS or disable the cache with INTEL_SIMILARITY_CACHE_MAX_AGE_SECS=0. A high `error` rate is harmless to correctness (a cache that cannot be read is treated as a miss) but means the live path is carrying all traffic.

panels.title: Similarity shed rate (bulkhead saturation)
panels.description: Share of similarity searches rejected by the in-process concurrency bulkhead (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED). Non-zero means INTEL_SIMILARITY_MAX_CONCURRENT is saturating. Raise it ONLY after confirming ClickHouse and the screening p50 have headroom — the ceiling exists precisely to stop this endpoint degrading GetScreeningFacts, which shares the same service and store and carries a p50 < 100ms SLO (§19). Shedding here is the system working, not failing.

panels.title: Clustering signal: what happened to each subject
panels.description: §20.3 t3. Every AddressEmbeddingUpdated the signal saw, by what it did with it. `searched` is the only outcome that costs a ClickHouse ANN scan — every other value is a gate refusing to run one. `already_clustered` dominating is the EXPECTED healthy shape with INTEL_LINK_SIGNAL_ONLY_UNCLUSTERED=true: the entity graph reached those addresses first, and the signal exists for the ones it cannot. `no_baseline` is the failure that looks like silence — nothing errors, the queue simply stops filling.

panels.title: Candidate links written
panels.description: By store outcome. `new` and `re_announce` are the two that publish EntityLinkProposed. `re_announce` is the CRASH WINDOW being covered: the row committed, the process died before the publish, and redelivery found it still owing its event — a small steady rate around deploys is the mechanism working, a sustained one means the pod is dying mid-pass. `refreshed` is the same link rediscovered and already announced (stronger evidence than a one-off, which is why last_seen_at is stored); `decided` is a proposal an operator already ruled on, left untouched so a rejection can never be reopened by a re-run. A healthy steady state is mostly `refreshed`.

panels.title: Why neighbours were not proposed
panels.description: The tuning panel for INTEL_LINK_MIN_SIMILARITY and label coverage. `below_threshold` is the overwhelming majority by design. `no_anchor` dominating means §8.1 label coverage is too thin for the signal to have anything to anchor on. `capped` dominating means the per-subject bound has become the actual selection criterion — raise the threshold, not the cap: the cap protects the queue, the threshold decides what deserves to be in it. `derived_anchor_only` is the second-order-taint refusal — a match onto a label the system itself guessed, never allowed to propose a further hop.

panels.title: Candidate-link listings served
panels.description: Reads of the proposal queue (GET /v1/address/{addr}/link-candidates, gRPC ListLinkCandidates) and how many proposals each returned. A cheap keyed read: the expensive work already happened in the link-signal consumer, which is exactly why the proposals are materialized rather than searched for on demand. Listings near zero while `new` proposals climb means the flywheel is writing leads nobody is triaging — the signal's value is realized by a human looking at it.
